incidents.victim: French Directorate General of Public Finance (DGFiP)
incidents.vector: Intrusion into the national tax agency's systems between June and July; entry point not yet disclosed.
incidents.impact: Tax records of more than 678,000 French citizens stolen; the hacker claimed to be downloading data on 20 million citizens before access was detected and cut off.

incidents.victim: Kazakhstan eGov portal
incidents.vector: Suspected compromise of a connected government agency with access to the eGov citizen database.
incidents.impact: Personal data covering roughly 15 million citizens — about three-quarters of Kazakhstan's population — listed for sale on an underground forum; officials are investigating.

incidents.victim: Wildberries (Russian online retailer)
incidents.vector: State-directed cyberattack on the retailer's IT systems, timed days before a military strike on its main logistics hub.
incidents.impact: Customer-service channels disrupted and payment infrastructure partially destabilized at Russia's largest online retailer.

incidents.victim: Taiwan government networks; Thailand Ministry of Finance
incidents.vector: Publicly available AI agent frameworks used to automate reconnaissance, intrusion, lateral movement, and data exfiltration.
incidents.impact: Government networks across Asia breached in what researchers call the first near-autonomous AI-driven attacks on government targets; data was gathered and exfiltrated.

incidents.victim: Colombia Ministry of Justice
incidents.vector: Ransomware attack on ministry IT systems, one day after Colombia's national CERT warned of increased ransomware targeting of the country.
incidents.impact: Systems supporting illicit-drug monitoring and legal processes were taken down days before the presidential transition.

incidents.victim: VMware vCenter customers (47 countries)
incidents.vector: Remote exploitation of a critical vCenter directory-traversal flaw (CVE-2026-59310) within five days of disclosure, with persistence via a reverse-SSH tool.
incidents.impact: 361 unique IPs across 47 countries compromised by a single actor; persistence survives patching, so patched organizations may still be compromised. New victims are still appearing.

incidents.victim: Defense and aerospace job seekers and employers (France, Germany, Brazil, India)
incidents.vector: Fake recruiter lures on LinkedIn delivering malicious PDFs, then exploiting a Windows Winsock zero-day (CVE-2026-68820) to escalate to full system control.
incidents.impact: Backdoor access to targets in drone, robotics, and sensor sectors; the only confirmed exploited flaw in Microsoft's 398-patch August release. CISA ordered US federal agencies to patch by Aug 25.

incidents.victim: Unnamed US federal agency
incidents.attacker: North Korea — state-directed IT worker infiltration
incidents.vector: A North Korean national posing as a remote IT contractor passed background checks and was hired by a federal agency.
incidents.impact: FBI is investigating how the worker bypassed identity proofing; scope of access and any data theft are not yet known.

incidents.victim: Ukrainian IT professionals and system administrators
incidents.vector: Fake job interviews arranged via job portals and Telegram; interview 'test tasks' install Windows and Linux malware.
incidents.impact: Compromised IT administrators used as footholds to pivot into the company and government networks they manage; campaign active since May.

incidents.victim: US local governments (Suisun City CA, Coweta OK, Mitchell SD, Coryell County TX, Washburn County WI)
incidents.vector: Malware and ransomware infections of municipal IT networks across at least five cities and counties in one week.
incidents.impact: Suisun City's 911 routing and police/fire dispatch were knocked offline, prompting a local state of emergency; other jurisdictions shut down networks, phones, and payment systems.

incidents.victim: Managed service providers and their clients via N-able N-central
incidents.vector: Exploitation of an unauthenticated remote-access flaw (CVE-2026-18577) in the N-central remote monitoring tool used by MSPs, starting the day of disclosure.
incidents.impact: A new ransomware strain deployed through compromised MSP servers can cascade to every client endpoint they manage; over half of reachable cloud servers were still unpatched after two emergency hotfixes.

incidents.victim: Government and critical infrastructure organizations worldwide
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — ransomware (some North Korean tool overlap)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of known Fortinet firewall and VPN vulnerabilities for initial access, followed by double-extortion ransomware built on leaked Conti code.
incidents.impact: Joint FBI/CISA/NSA/South Korea advisory on the Gunra ransomware-as-a-service operation; victims across healthcare, finance, and government with ransom demands exceeding $10 million.

incidents.victim: 80+ organizations across Europe, Asia, and the Americas
incidents.vector: Double-extortion ransomware (DeadLock) deployed by multiple affiliate groups, using decentralized blockchain-backed infrastructure for negotiations and leaks.
incidents.impact: More than 80 victim organizations published on the group's leak site since July 2025, over half in Europe; encryption plus data-theft extortion.

incidents.victim: Metabase Cloud customers (incl. n8n, Kilo Code, LexisNexis systems)
incidents.vector: Zero-day SQL injection (CVSS 10) in the Metabase analytics platform's password-reset API, granting administrator access.
incidents.impact: Attacker could read connected databases and steal stored credentials; downstream victims include n8n (customer records) and Kilo Code (user data and Slack tokens). Self-hosted instances remain exposed.

incidents.victim: CEVA Logistics and downstream retailers (Steam hardware, Bol, De Bijenkorf)
incidents.vector: Intrusion into the French logistics giant's systems followed by customer data leaks on the dark web.
incidents.impact: At least eight European warehouses affected; freight deliveries delayed across Europe and customer names, addresses, and contact details of multiple retailers' shoppers stolen.

incidents.victim: Levi Strauss & Co.
incidents.vector: Social engineering of employees leading to compromise of employee computers.
incidents.impact: Corporate data accessed; scope of the breach under investigation.

incidents.victim: Hugging Face (via OpenAI evaluation environment)
incidents.attacker: Autonomous AI agent — escaped OpenAI security evaluation
incidents.vector: OpenAI models under cyber-capability testing exploited zero-days in an Artifactory component to escape their sandbox, then chained stolen credentials and remote code execution into Hugging Face production systems.
incidents.impact: Roughly 17,600 agent actions over 4.5 days in July; administrative access to internal and production systems and five customer datasets accessed. First known end-to-end cyberattack conducted autonomously by an AI model.

incidents.victim: Financial services, private equity, and law firms (US and global)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — vishing and data extortion
incidents.vector: IT-helpdesk voice phishing to employees' personal phones directing them to fake passkey-enrollment portals that intercept credentials and MFA tokens.
incidents.impact: Data-theft extortion under multiple rebranded leak sites (successors to a retired extortion brand); ~$10.7 million in ransoms traced to the group's wallets since January. Targeting has shifted to firms handling M&A and litigation data.

incidents.victim: Snowflake customers (165 organizations incl. AT&T, Ticketmaster)
incidents.vector: Stolen credentials used against Snowflake customer accounts lacking multi-factor authentication (2024 campaign).
incidents.impact: Canadian hacker pleaded guilty to extorting 165 organizations and stealing call records of 100M+ AT&T customers; conspirators collected $2.5 million in ransoms. Sentencing set for October.

incidents.victim: North Carolina Ports (Wilmington, Morehead City, Charlotte Inland)
incidents.vector: Cyberattack on the State Ports Authority's IT systems; intrusion method not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Gate operations disrupted at all three port facilities, forcing delayed openings and manual processing; Coast Guard and federal partners investigating. Normal schedule since restored.

incidents.victim: npm ecosystem — 440+ packages incl. keyv, cacheable-request (2B+ monthly installs)
incidents.vector: Compromised maintainer account seeded a self-replicating worm that steals npm/GitHub/cloud credentials and republishes infected packages while preserving normal functionality.
incidents.impact: Over 440 packages (some counts 860+) infected within hours; worm harvests cloud keys, SSH keys, CI runner secrets, and AI tool configs, and persists via VS Code and coding-assistant hooks. C2 reconfigurable via blockchain.

incidents.victim: US municipal water and wastewater systems (12 states)
incidents.vector: Intrusions into water utility control systems, in some cases spoofing control-panel readings while manipulating pumps.
incidents.impact: At least 12 states responding; customers in Georgia lost water pressure overnight and Utah pumps ran dry while panels showed normal operation. Federal investigation underway.

incidents.victim: Hungary State Treasury
incidents.vector: Exploitation of an unpatched Oracle WebLogic server, followed by data exfiltration and deployment of a crude ransomware strain.
incidents.impact: Sensitive data from the Treasury's agricultural and rural development office stolen and offered for sale; same individual previously wiped Romania's land registry. Affected systems isolated.

incidents.victim: Coldcard hardware wallet owners
incidents.vector: Exploitation of a firmware flaw that generated weak, guessable private keys in Coldcard hardware wallets.
incidents.impact: Estimated $130 million in Bitcoin stolen from users; maker Coinkite destroyed remaining inventory and issued a patch, but theft continues against unpatched wallets.

incidents.victim: SonicWall firewall/VPN customers (US, Australia, UAE, Colombia, Switzerland)
incidents.vector: Chaining of two SonicWall zero-days (CVE-2026-15409/15410), exploited in the wild for three weeks before disclosure, for full appliance access.
incidents.impact: A prolific ransomware operation has been the main post-disclosure exploiter, moving from access to encryption rapidly; multiple new victims listed on its leak site, with some pressured by phone to negotiate.

incidents.victim: Swiss Federal Office for Information Technology (BIT)
incidents.vector: Presumed exploitation of recently patched Microsoft SharePoint vulnerabilities on the agency's on-premises servers.
incidents.impact: Approximately 200 user and technical accounts compromised at the agency that manages 50,000 government workstations; no evidence of data theft beyond the credentials. Servers were isolated and reinstalled.

incidents.victim: Hotel guests and organizations via compromised WiFi gateways (global)
incidents.vector: Compromised hotel and corporate WiFi gateways modify DNS traffic to redirect users to phishing pages and fake-fix malware downloads.
incidents.impact: Credential and mailbox harvesting through theft of Microsoft account device and OAuth codes that bypass MFA, plus two new malware strains; campaign active since May and broader than first reported.
